findings.title: Fireworks October 2026 security incident
findings.summary_md: Fireworks published its first incident bulletin after detecting unauthorized use of internal Fireworks credentials on October 6, 2026 at 9:00 AM PDT. The unauthorized third party accessed environment variables used in evaluation jobs in a limited number of customer accounts, capturing API keys and tokens stored as secrets. The company revoked internal credentials, rotated employee API keys on October 9, notified affected customers, and revoked additional user API keys and rotated service-account tokens on October 10. At publication the company said it had found no evidence of access to customer models, datasets, training data, inference traffic, or personal information within its security perimeter.

findings.title: The Rise of LLMJacking: How Threat Actors Monetize Compromised Cloud and Model Resources
findings.summary_md: Google Threat Intelligence Group and Mandiant documented LLMJacking, the hijacking of enterprise access to large language models, based on multiple 2026 incident responses across North America, South America, and Asia Pacific in financial services, retail, technology, and transportation. The report records fraudulent charges above 100,000 USD in a single day in some incidents and cumulative charges approaching 1 million USD at some organizations. It describes financially motivated clusters and downstream operators running LLM Mixers, illicit routing gateways that proxy, aggregate, and resell unauthorized LLM access to underground subscribers. Dominant initial access was exposed or stolen cloud identity tokens, including IAM credentials, service account keys, GitHub personal access tokens, and active session tokens.

findings.title: Update on October 2026 security incident
findings.summary_md: Fireworks expanded its October bulletin after forensics with Palo Alto Networks Unit 42, confirming impact to account and billing information and, for a limited set of accounts, secrets, datasets, and incomplete model weights. The bulletin attributes the activity to a financially motivated cybercriminal group linked to LLMJacking and cites the Google Threat Intelligence Group and Mandiant report published November 2. It states a third-party cloud provider hosting Fireworks R&D machines had an incident on October 23, that the actor used it on October 24 to reach Fireworks development machines and run an unauthorized workload, that Fireworks detected and remediated the same day, and that no further successful unauthorized access was detected as of October 25. Fireworks disabled self-serve dataset uploads and downloads used by batch inference and dataset-based training during the investigation.

findings.title: Fireworks AI incident
findings.summary_md: Notion published an advisory stating Fireworks notified it on November 2 that a small set of data had been accessed, which Notion initially assessed as Notion AI synthetic testing data with no customer data involved. By the morning of November 3 Notion disconnected from Fireworks, deleted its data in the Fireworks system, and stopped communication; Fireworks notified Notion on November 6 that customer data may have been accessed and confirmed the final impacted dataset on November 8. The dataset contained Notion AI chat transcripts used for the Insights feature, and Notion reached out to impacted customers on November 9. Fewer than 1 percent of Notion workspaces were affected, most transcripts were unattributable to a workspace or user, the Insights feature was disabled, and Notion revoked exposed Notion API keys found in affected user messages on November 11.

findings.title: Fireworks AI gets burned twice as customer data exposure widens
findings.summary_md: The Register reported Fireworks' second October incident and the wider customer data exposure involving billing records, datasets, and incomplete model weights. It states a third-party cloud provider hosting the company's research and development machines was compromised on October 23 and that attackers used that access the next day to reach Fireworks development systems and run an unauthorized workload. Fireworks suspects links to financially motivated criminals involved in LLMJacking, selling unauthorized access to AI models, and notes the first incident was disclosed on October 9 after detection on October 6.

findings.title: Fireworks AI discloses new breach after cloud provider hack
findings.summary_md: BleepingComputer reported the second Fireworks breach, in which attackers accessed development machines after breaching a third-party cloud provider. The article repeats the bulletin's attribution to a financially motivated cybercriminal group selling LLM tokens to illicit routing gateways, and notes the earlier October incident involved environment variables containing API keys and tokens stored as secrets for a limited number of accounts. It confirms incomplete model weights and datasets were reachable for some customers while payment card numbers were not stored by Fireworks and were not impacted.
